g1-implement.title: #604 telemetry-never-fatal: implement
g1-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md for gate g1 and dispatch constellation-implementer through scripts/run_crew.py. TASK: make the door's telemetry writes incapable of failing a tool call or the server process. `_log` (scripts/mcp_spine_server.py:180) opens CALLLOG unguarded and `run_engine` calls it at :461 OUTSIDE its own try/except; main() catches only KeyError at :1355/:1360, so any OSError from the log write unwinds the whole process. START_MARKER.write_text (:184) has the same exposure. The fix shape ALREADY EXISTS in this module -- `_log_rejection` (:472) wraps its write, reports the loss to stderr, and never raises; reuse that shape rather than inventing a second one. Catch OSError (covering FileNotFoundError, PermissionError, IsADirectoryError), not bare Exception. stderr is safe: stdout is the JSON-RPC channel (main() writes protocol to sys.stdout only, :1367/:1375). SECOND DELIVERABLE, and it is not optional (critic finding 4, measured): a COMMITTED REGRESSION TEST that FAILS on the pre-fix tree and passes after -- a subprocess whose exit code is asserted with the telemetry path pointed at an unwritable location. Demonstrate it failing on the pre-fix tree; do not assert that it would. Without it this gate's pytest postcondition passes identically on the healthy and the defective tree (measured: 89 passed on the UNFIXED tree) and #604 can return the day after merge. Integrate the returned IMPLEMENTER_RESULT: `attach g1-implement --type implementer-result --field status=<verbatim lowercase Return status>`.

g2-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md for gate g2 and dispatch constellation-implementer through scripts/run_crew.py. GATE ORDER NOTE: this gate runs BEFORE the #603 binding gate, reversing the launch order's presentation sequence. Reason, from critic finding 8 and adopted deliberately: g3 removes .mcp.json's demo default, so demo-first means the shipped default never points at a broken file at ANY commit, and g3 then owns the README sentence its own change falsifies. TASK: examples/mcp-interactive-demo/spine.json is tracked, ships to every install, and carries six absolute paths (lines 20/28/78/86/109/117) into /home/tommy/projects/constellation-skills-wt/f-424 -- a worktree deleted during the epic-418-followon closeout, on one machine, which never existed anywhere else. MEASURED CONSTRAINT THAT OVERRIDES THE ISSUE'S OWN FIX DIRECTION (critic finding 6, verified): #605 and decision:demo-spine-is-generated-not-hand-fixed both say 'paths relative to the example directory'. That CANNOT WORK -- checklist_engine.py:883 runs command checks with `subprocess.run([shell, '-c', command])` and NO cwd, so a relative path resolves against whatever directory the driving process happens to stand in (through the door: the bound spine's git toplevel; from the CLI: the user's cwd). Relative-to-the-example-directory resolves correctly from essentially nowhere. The surviving generator, which already recorded this reasoning, is at .agent-work/archive/2026-08-09-epic-418-followon/commander-424/crew-plans/scratch-mcp/make_scratch_spine.py ('Command-check paths are ABSOLUTE (the engine runs command checks with no cwd)'). Honor decision:demo-spine-is-generated-not-hand-fixed -- do NOT hand-edit the six strings. ALSO: say where the demo's `<arm>/workspace/` writes land; regenerating under examples/ would dirty a tracked directory. THEN add the guard #605 asks for: a real test in the suite that keeps a machine-specific absolute path out of a shipped example. It MUST FAIL on the current file -- demonstrate that, do not assert it. Integrate the returned IMPLEMENTER_RESULT: `attach g2-implement --type implementer-result --field status=<verbatim lowercase Return status>`.

g3-implement.title: #603 fail-closed and bind-on-open: implement
g3-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md for gate g3 and dispatch constellation-implementer through scripts/run_crew.py. This is the run's hardest gate. TWO changes that compose. (A) FAIL CLOSED. Treat UNSET, EMPTY, non-existent, non-file and unreadable as ONE 'unbound' class, and make every tool answer a refusal instead of a demo answer, a crash, or silence. Three distinct failure worlds are MEASURED on the current tree, and the naive fix only addresses one: SPINE_FILE unset -> EXIT 1, KeyError at :146, server dies AT IMPORT, client sees 'Connection closed'; SPINE_FILE='' -> Path('').resolve() is the CWD, server starts and answers `IsADirectoryError: Is a directory: <repo root>`, EXIT 0; SPINE_FILE=<missing path> -> #604's crash before g1. The empty case is the one PRODUCTION WILL TAKE: .mcp.json's form is `${SPINE_FILE:-<default>}` and tests/test_mcp_spine_server.py:574 pins that the key is present, so dropping the default yields `${SPINE_FILE:-}`, which expands to EMPTY, not unset. Also make ENGINE (:145, SPINE_ENGINE) fail closed in the same motion -- measured: unset SPINE_ENGINE is a KeyError at import too, and a session with no SPINE_FILE very likely has no SPINE_ENGINE either. Refusal wording splits (critic finding 10): an UNBOUND refusal cannot name a path that does not exist -- say 'no spine is bound; call spine_open (or set SPINE_FILE)'; a MISSING/UNREADABLE refusal names the path AND says how to rebind. (B) BIND ON OPEN, per decision:bind-on-open-over-new-verb. THE MEASURED COST, established -- do not rediscover: four import-time derivations of SPINE must become late-bound -- CALLLOG (:162), START_MARKER (:167), REJECTIONLOG (:177), and _resolve_confined's `bound_dir: Path = SPINE.parent` DEFAULT ARGUMENT (:188), evaluated once at import and the subtlest of the four. An independent AST pass confirmed there is no fifth. But TWO further roots the four-item list excludes, both proved by the critic: (i) `_primary_checkout_for_lifecycle` (:593) does its OWN hard `os.environ['SPINE_FILE']` read, and _spine_open calls it at :657 inside `except (OSError, RuntimeError)`, which does NOT catch KeyError -- so after (A) lands, an unbound session calling spine_open gets `tool error: missing or unknown 'SPINE_FILE'`, and the exit criterion is NOT reached. PREFERRED ANSWER, and it is this gate's to confirm or reject with reasons: derive the primary checkout from the SERVER SCRIPT'S OWN LOCATION (Path(__file__).resolve()), then `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` from there -- it needs no new env var, no ambient cwd read, and does not reintroduce what :568-592 argues against. If that does not hold, STOP and report rather than adding a fourth ambient input. (ii) `open_work` returns THREE binding values (spine_lifecycle.py:334-340: SPINE_FILE, SPINE_SESSION, SPINE_PARENT). Binding SPINE alone leaves SESSION empty, run_engine then omits --session-id (:442), and checklist_engine.py:1073 refuses `claim requires a non-empty --session-id` -- so the bound session cannot drive anything. REBIND SESSION from open_work's returned SPINE_SESSION too. RULED for this gate: a rebind is REFUSED while this process still holds an active lease on the current spine -- that preserves one-spine-per-process and prevents orphaning a lease; implement and test that refusal. THE PIN (critic finding 7, and its correction to the earlier framing): tests/test_mcp_lifecycle.py:194's identifier ban is over _spine_open's OWN source, so a module-level binder that _spine_open calls leaves it passing UNWEAKENED -- its letter and its spirit both survive. So KEEP :194 AND ITS POSITIVE CONTROL BYTE-IDENTICAL and ADD a new, strictly stronger assertion: an AST pin over the WHOLE MODULE that the set of assignments to SPINE and to SESSION is exactly {module scope, the one named binder}, with its own mutated positive control. That catches the real regression -- a second, quieter rebind site -- which a _spine_open-scoped ban cannot see. Do NOT rewrite :194 into a softer intent-shaped statement. Integrate the returned IMPLEMENTER_RESULT: `attach g3-implement --type implementer-result --field status=<verbatim lowercase Return status>`.
